title: Upgrade guide
html:
Upgrading MDK 0.14.0 → 0.15.0

Scope and provenance

This guide compares v0.14.0 / marmotkit-v0.14.0 / marmotc-v0.14.0 / wn-agent-v0.14.0, which all peel to 3fb4b4759ac676b0c21c4c3527074866c9fa4c89, with the source to be shipped as v0.15.0. All four 0.15.0 cohort tags must peel to the release PR's merged commit, and packaged manifests must record that exact SHA. The comparison was prepared against origin/master at 1a5d7d419341f7b205362c25b6166ed2252c7be7; use the full release SHA from the tags for artifact verification. This guide ships in the release commit, not a later supplement. See the release notes, previous upgrade guide, and current binding reference.

Readers: native app hosts (Swift/Kotlin through MarmotKit), C hosts, Rust hosts that embed marmot-app or lower crates, and WN Agent operators.

Unlike 0.14.0, this release changes what devices put on the wire: KeyPackages and leaves advertise the account-devices component, new groups can require it, KeyPackages are refreshed weekly, push-token records are exchanged more often, and automatic rejoin adds an account-inbox handshake. The conformance vectors add the account-devices-* scenarios and a large-Welcome NIP-44 fixture. The new formal models cover experimental device pairing and linking only.

Upgrade decisions

Category Required action or effect
Required Replace generated Swift/Kotlin, native libraries and C headers together. Update TimelineMessageQueryFfi construction (four new fields with no default) and remove MarmotDeploymentFfi.keyPackagePreferredClients / keyPackageLastClients. Handle 22 new MarmotKitError cases, 8 new MarmotEventFfi cases, WelcomeDeliveryPending.sizeClass and new enum cases. Re-upload media references saved by 0.14.0.
Required for C hosts Recompile. Several structs gain fields mid-struct (MarmotMediaAttachmentReference, message/timeline/preview/notification records, MarmotTimelineMessageRecord). Statuses 108–129 and enum values are appended; none is renumbered. marmot_deployment_set_key_package_client_preference is removed.
Required storage Keep a device-local copy, then allow account migrations 0117–0153, 0160–0180, 0200 and 0201 (schema 116 → 201) on first open. Downgrade is unsupported.
Required for Rust hosts cgka-session is now marmot-session; handle the API changes in Rust host changes. Building from source needs Odin.
New defaults Account-devices component on new groups (0.14 clients cannot be invited into them later), every device of an account invited, members listed per account, 30-day KeyPackages refreshed weekly, sign-out deletes only this device's slot, signOutAndWipe steps an admin down and leaves, recovery runner owns history, automatic rejoin, more push-token gossip, admin invitees step down before declining, MultiDeviceUnsupported no longer produced, ordinary constructors refuse device-group accounts, wider preview lookup, identity-proof reuse.
Optional adoption Chat-list filtered queries and select-all, timeline search filters, stickers, emoji sets, blocked-leave Cancel, pending Welcome deliveries, custom reaction artwork, account recovery status, account-devices activation.
Automatic fixes Offline sends publish after reconnect and keep their order, Welcomes wait for their Commit, convergence retries back off, refused queued intents retire, oversized events report EventTooLarge, cheaper idle ticks, wnd memory leak, faster cached user search, security updates.

Required upgrade steps

  1. Pin all MDK, MarmotKit, Marmot C and WN Agent inputs to 0.15.0. Verify the source SHA in each manifest and every sibling checksum. Do not combine new generated records or headers with 0.14.0 native libraries. See the distribution guide.

  2. Update host-built records:

    • TimelineMessageQueryFfi gains sender, since, until and cursorGroupId with no binding defaults, plus attachmentType (default 0) and searchWallClock (default false). They are declared before before, so positional Kotlin calls shift. See Timeline search filters.
    • MarmotDeploymentFfi drops keyPackagePreferredClients and keyPackageLastClients; delete those assignments. Invite candidates are no longer ranked by KeyPackage client.
    • MarmotOptions gains devicePlatform (default nil) between clientName and secretStore. It only labels this device for experimental device groups.
    • Output records gain fields without defaults, breaking host-built mocks and previews: AccountSummaryFfi.unlinked; leaveBlocked and canCancelLeave on group, chat-row, management and capability records; sticker: StickerRefFfi? on message, received, notification, chat-preview, timeline and reply-preview records; recipientConfirmed, importedFrom and historyImportProvenance on TimelineMessageRecordFfi; two new WipeOutcomeFfi fields. deviceCount, convergenceParked and MediaAttachmentReferenceFfi.sourceEpochIdentity have defaults.

  3. Update exhaustive handling:

    • MarmotKitError gains MediaReferenceStaleEpoch, MediaReferenceEpochUnsettled, EventTooLarge { artifact, sizeClass }, LeaveNotBlocked, AccountDevicesActivationRefused, InvalidChatListQuery { reason }, AccountUnlinked, GroupRecoveryUnsettled, GroupRecoverySourceMismatch, five Sticker* errors and eight EmojiSet*/EmojiImage* errors.
    • Remapped failures: busy, closed or full storage and a rejected external-signer prompt that reached the host as Runtime now arrive as StorageBusy, StorageClosed, StorageFull and ExternalSignerRejected. Wipe-outcome reason strings follow the underlying error, whichever layer wrapped it: local storage error, unknown local group, account is the chat's last admin (AdminDepletion), account is an admin of the chat (AdminCannotSelfRemove), session error for any other engine failure, or account error; an event every relay refused for size (Publish or Runtime) is EventTooLarge; a media send at the wrong epoch (InvalidMediaReference) is MediaReferenceStaleEpoch or MediaReferenceEpochUnsettled.
    • MarmotEventFfi gains RecoveryStatusChanged, DeviceUnlinked, LinkedDevicesChanged, KeyPackageRefreshOverdueChanged, UnrecognizedSignInsChanged, CompromiseWarningChanged, DeviceLinkChanged and ChatHistoryImportsChanged. Every case except RecoveryStatusChanged belongs to experimental device groups: MDK sends them only when device groups are on, so ordinary hosts never see them, but exhaustive switches still need the arms.
    • WelcomeDeliveryPending gains sizeClass: EventSizeClassFfi?. HistoryNoticeCauseFfi gains UnprovenHistory and BeforeRejoin; SelfMembershipFfi and ConversationParticipationFfi gain DeviceRemoved; GroupEventKindFfi gains QueuedIntentRefused.

    No existing exported method was removed, renamed or changed between sync and async, and callbacks are unchanged. Compare with the v0.14.0 method reference.

  4. Media references saved by 0.14.0 have no sourceEpochIdentity. Sending one fails with MediaReferenceStaleEpoch and publishes nothing; upload the retained bytes again. Saved and received references stay downloadable. Preserve sourceEpochIdentity unchanged wherever you store an upload result.

  5. Recompile C consumers against the regenerated marmot.h. See C host changes.

  6. Keep a device-local copy of each account directory before first open. See Storage upgrade.

  7. Update localized copy for the onboarding SingleDevice notice and new prompts (blocked leave, admin invitee decline, catching up). See Changed defaults.

  8. Rust hosts: see Rust host changes. WN Agent operators: see WN Agent and integrations.

Illustrative Swift for the new event field and errors:

switch event {
case let .welcomeDeliveryPending(accountIdHex, _, groupIdHex, _, recipientHex, sizeClass):
    showWelcomePending(accountIdHex, groupIdHex, recipientHex, tooLarge: sizeClass != nil)
case .recoveryStatusChanged(let accountIdHex, _):
    refreshRecoveryStatus(accountIdHex)
case .linkedDevicesChanged, .keyPackageRefreshOverdueChanged, .unrecognizedSignInsChanged,
     .compromiseWarningChanged, .deviceLinkChanged, .chatHistoryImportsChanged:
    break // experimental device groups only
default:
    handleExisting(event)
}

do {
    try await marmot.sendMediaAttachments(accountRef: account, groupIdHex: group,
                                          attachments: refs, caption: nil)
} catch MarmotKitError.MediaReferenceStaleEpoch {
    promptReupload() // nothing was published
} catch MarmotKitError.MediaReferenceEpochUnsettled {
    retryLater()
}

Kotlin equivalents are is MarmotEventFfi.WelcomeDeliveryPending -> event.sizeClass and catch (e: MarmotKitException.MediaReferenceStaleEpoch).

Storage upgrade

Schema migrations

Account databases (session.sqlite) advance from schema 116 to 201 on first open through migrations 0117–0153, 0160–0180, 0200 and 0201 (the gaps are unused numbers). Each migration runs in its own transaction, so an interrupted upgrade resumes where it stopped. Tables for experimental device groups are created but stay empty in ordinary builds.

No migration copies or rebuilds app_events or message_timeline. A few scan history-sized tables once, so a large account's first open takes longer and needs temporary disk for the WAL and new indexes:

  • 0167 backfills attachment sources from stored custom-emoji reactions.
  • 0141 adds last_message_tags_json to chat-list rows, so the first open after upgrade rebuilds the chat-list projection of almost every account.
  • 0169 adds columns and builds eight indexes on the processed transport-id table, which has one row per processed event; 0174 drops those indexes again in the same upgrade and leaves the unused columns in place.
  • 0173 rebuilds the chat-preview index over message_timeline and marks failed own sends a peer has reacted to as delivered (recipientConfirmed).
  • 0175 decodes every saved outbound fanout and group evolution to seed a pending-reference watermark. An undecodable row aborts the migration, and the account does not open, rather than risking a reused reference.
  • 0180 reads stored moderation-removal events once, records the validation state and hold targets of each, and blanks the bodies of pruned removals whose original decision could not be proved. Nothing keeps a copy of a blanked body, including a valid decision that could no longer be proved.
  • With native push on, 0117 queues a push-registration share for every joined group, so the first open after upgrade republishes once per group.
  • 0120, 0153, 0179 and 0200 work per group or per chat: member counts become account counts, each group records its current copy for recovery, chat rows gain their kind, and the presentation dependency table is rebuilt.

0200 invalidates every stored chat presentation once. Rows keep rendering their last value while the account's presentation worker rewrites them, but until it finishes a query with a Text node fails with ChatPresentationNotReady. 0136 adds the one-time conversion of the old recovery rows; the account worker runs it after open, not inside the migration.

This guide has no measurement of the 116 → 201 upgrade on a large account. Account startup now gives up only after 45 seconds without progress rather than 45 seconds in total, so a slow first open that is still migrating no longer fails startup. If a notification extension can be the first process to open an account after upgrade, it runs these migrations inside its own time and memory budget; test that path and prefer letting the main app open first.

The per-account directory cache (app-cache.sqlite3) stays at schema 2, and the shared shared.sqlite3 schema is unchanged.

Downgrade and backups

Downgrade is unsupported. A 0.14.0 binary refuses a migrated database with UnsupportedSchemaVersion before reading application tables, and older readers cannot decode the new stored-message variants. The remedies are to re-upgrade or to restore a device-local copy of the account directory taken before upgrading: the databases with their WAL, the .salt sidecars, media/, and the secret-store credentials. Restoring an older copy also rewinds MLS state, so prefer re-upgrading. Keep excluding the account directory from cloud and device backups.

See the storage-format contract and local artifact safety.

Changed defaults

Accounts with several devices

  • Every 0.15 build advertises marmot.group.account-devices.v1 (0x800d) in its KeyPackages and leaves. A new group requires it when the creating device and every device added at creation advertise it, and that requirement is permanent: a client that does not advertise it, including 0.14.0 and older, cannot be invited into the group later, and no account may hold more than 20 devices in it. A group created with a 0.14.0 founder is created as before. Existing groups are unchanged until an admin calls enableAccountDevices (see Account-devices activation).
  • Creating a group or inviting adds every device of each recipient account: up to 20 valid KeyPackages published in the last 30 days, or the single best valid one when none is that recent. Lookup is best effort; see known limitations. Inviting the inviter's own account is refused before anything is sent (Runtime), as creating a group already was.
  • A device joins only through the Welcome that names its own KeyPackage.
  • Member rows, rosters, conversation snapshots, memberCount, admin counts and direct-chat detection count accounts, not leaves. A member row's deviceCount says how many of that account's devices are in the group. A group-system row marks only an account's first device joining or its last device leaving. See Members are accounts.

KeyPackages and sign-out

  • New KeyPackages are valid for 30 days (0.14.0: 84), and each device replaces its own every 6 to 7 days while it runs and after a Welcome uses it. Expect more KeyPackage publishing.
  • signOutAndWipe and sign-out delete only this device's KeyPackage slot with one kind-5 deletion, instead of every KeyPackage the account published. keyPackagesDeleted on SignOutOutcomeFfi and WipeOutcomeFfi is now 1 when a relay accepted that deletion, otherwise 0.
  • signOutAndWipe now also leaves chats the account administers. In a chat where another account is an active admin and no other device of this account remains, it steps the account down and leaves, waiting up to about 30 seconds for a commit that removes this device. A last admin, or an admin whose other device stays in the chat, keeps its leaf and is reported in groupLeaveFailures. Their reason strings are new: account is the chat's last admin, account is an admin of the chat, account is an admin and another of its devices stays in the chat, account's step-down as admin was not accepted in time and account is not an admin and its removal was not seen in time. The call keeps running when the caller cancels; show progress rather than assuming an instant return. Plain signOut is unchanged: it keeps chat membership and admin rights.
  • A clientName over 64 bytes is left off the KeyPackage.
  • Reopening an account reuses its stored, validated identity proof, so a NIP-46/Amber signer is no longer asked to sign again on every reopen.

Recovery and automatic rejoin

  • The recovery runner owns account history. Catch-up after time offline is bounded and paced, history arrives in order, and a group's newer live messages wait until its fetched backlog is admitted, so they can appear slightly later after a reconnect. Notification wakes fetch only the history their messages wait on. RecoveryStatusChanged and UnprovenHistory notices are now produced; see Account recovery status.
  • Account workers rejoin a group copy that became Unrecoverable through an authenticated handshake with an admin device over the account inbox, with bounded retries. The existing Repair action rearms a parked attempt; restarting does not reset its budget. Usable forks still need the user's consent. A rejoined group raises one BeforeRejoin notice: messages from before the rejoin that the device had not received are unavailable. See the automatic rejoin contract.

Leaving and invitations as an admin

requiresSelfDemoteBeforeLeave is now also true for an admin invitee with a pending invitation: declineGroupInvite returns AdminCannotSelfRemove until selfDemoteAdmin succeeds. Admin Leave is still refused until self-demotion, as in 0.14.0. A leave that later becomes blocked is now shown; see Blocked leaves.

Other defaults

  • Push notifications reach every device of a member, members added later learn existing tokens, and devices repair missed tokens inside each group. This adds push-token traffic (kinds 447–449) after Adds and on repair; no API change.
  • Onboarding no longer produces OnboardingIssueFfi.MultiDeviceUnsupported (the case remains), and the SingleDevice step explains what signing in alone restores. Update the copy as the README's Single-device notice shows.
  • resolvePublicEventPreview asks the deployment's discovery indexers and up to four cached author write relays (eight relays at most) once more when relay hints and directory relays miss, so pasted note1, hex and author-only nevent references resolve. Neutral deployments dial no indexer.
  • sendCustomEvent refuses device-group kinds 457–461, 473, 475 and 476.
  • Timeline search lowercases non-ASCII text, so école finds ÉCOLE.
  • Ordinary constructors refuse an account that holds or is joining a device group: its session fails with Runtime experimental_device_groups_required. Only roots previously opened by an experimental build are affected; see Experimental device groups.

Feature adoption

These are local unless stated; call them off the UI thread. MarmotKit's threading model is unchanged.

Chat-list queries and select all (optional)

Filter the chat list and select every chat a filter matches, for folders and bulk actions. See Chat-list select all and filtered queries.

  • openChatListQueryWindow(accountRef, query, initialRows) is openChatListWindow narrowed by ChatListViewQueryFfi { view, filter }. filter is a flat ChatListFilterNodeFfi list: node 0 is the root and every other node is the child of exactly one earlier node. All, Any and Not combine Condition (ChatListConditionFfi: Unread, Pinned, Archived, Direct, Group, Muted, HasDraft, PendingSend and more), GroupIds, Text and MessageText. The existing openChatListWindow is unchanged and equals an unfiltered query.
  • chatListQueryIds(accountRef, query) and chatListIds(accountRef, view) return every matching chat ID in display order, beyond any window; use the length as the count. Call revalidateChatListQueryIds (or revalidateChatListIds) right before a bulk action: it returns the subset still matching, in your order, and never adds chats. Then run the existing per-chat commands.
  • Limits: 64 nodes, 8 levels, 500 group IDs and 1024 bytes of text, refused with InvalidChatListQuery { reason: ChatListQueryErrorFfi } before any read. A window refuses MessageText (MessageTextInWindow) because it scans history.
  • While rows or presentation are still being prepared (after migration 0200, for example), the ID queries and any query with a Text node fail with ChatPresentationNotReady rather than return a partial list; retry.

Illustrative Kotlin (unread groups, excluding some):

val query = ChatListViewQueryFfi(
    view = ChatListViewFfi.CHATS,
    filter = listOf(
        ChatListFilterNodeFfi.All(children = listOf(1u, 2u, 3u)),
        ChatListFilterNodeFfi.Condition(ChatListConditionFfi.UNREAD),
        ChatListFilterNodeFfi.Condition(ChatListConditionFfi.GROUP),
        ChatListFilterNodeFfi.Not(child = 4u),
        ChatListFilterNodeFfi.GroupIds(groupIds = excludedIds),
    ),
)
val window = marmot.openChatListQueryWindow(account, query, null)
val selected = marmot.chatListQueryIds(account, query)
// later, before archiving:
val stillMatching = marmot.revalidateChatListQueryIds(account, query, selected)

Timeline search filters (optional)

timelineMessages(accountRef, query) can filter by sender (any form normalizeMemberRef accepts), inclusive since and exclusive until (Unix seconds) and attachmentType (0 Any, 1 Image, 2 Video, 3 Audio, 4 File, 5 any attachment; other values return Runtime). Filters combine with AND before the page limit; the existing 200-row page cap applies. searchWallClock = true orders by (timelineAt, messageIdHex, groupIdHex); to continue an account-wide wall-clock search, pass the last row's group as cursorGroupId with before/beforeMessageId. Keep filters unchanged between pages. subscribeTimelineMessages is unchanged. The call is synchronous and local, so run it off the UI thread. See Advanced timeline search.

Illustrative Swift (every caller must now pass the four new optional fields):

let query = TimelineMessageQueryFfi(
    groupIdHex: group, search: "invoice", sender: nil,
    since: startOfMonth, until: nil, attachmentType: 4,
    cursorGroupId: nil, before: nil, beforeMessageId: nil,
    after: nil, afterMessageId: nil, limit: 50)
let page = try marmot.timelineMessages(accountRef: account, query: query)

Stickers (optional)

Sonar-compatible packs: syncStickerPacks and fetchStickerPack use the network; stickerPacks and stickerPack are synchronous local reads; installStickerPack / uninstallStickerPack edit the published installed list. Render a message's sticker: StickerRefFfi? with fetchStickerAsset, never by fetching a URL yourself, and send with sendSticker(accountRef, groupIdHex, stickerRef). importSignalStickerPack validates a Signal link and then refuses with StickerImport. See Stickers.

Emoji sets (optional)

NIP-51 kind-30030 sets. syncEmojiSets, fetchEmojiSet, emojiSets, emojiSet and userEmojiList never download images. Image downloads reveal the user's IP address to hosts the set's author chose, so call fetchEmojiSetAsset, fetchEmojiSetCover and installEmojiSet only after the user acts. installEmojiSet(accountRef, coordinate, expectedEventIdHex, control) stores the version the user was shown (another fails with EmojiSetChanged before any download). Create an EmojiSetInstallControlFfi() per install, read progress(), and cancel() from any thread; a cancelled install fails with EmojiSetInstallCancelled and stores nothing. Caps: 50 sets, 500 emoji and 32 MiB per set, 128 MiB in all (EmojiSetLimit). Send an installed emoji by uploading readInstalledCustomEmoji bytes as an attachment. See Emoji sets.

Custom reaction artwork (optional)

reactionAttachment(accountRef, groupIdHex, reactionMessageIdHex) resolves an active custom-emoji reaction's encrypted artwork to an AttachmentEntryFfi, or nil. It is a bounded local read and starts no download; acquire the returned source slot with the existing attachment calls. Custom-emoji reaction sends are bound to their upload branch like media sends.

Blocked leaves (optional)

If the selected branch makes the account the group's last active admin after a leave was accepted (two admins left at once, say), the leave cannot finish. The chat keeps reading as leaving, and leaveBlocked is set on the group record, the chat-list row and management state. While canCancelLeave holds, offer Cancel: cancelLeave(accountRef, groupIdHex) clears the leave on this device only and the chat reads as joined again. In any other state it fails with LeaveNotBlocked. MDK never retries or reverses the leave by itself. See the README's leave contract under Linked devices.

Illustrative Swift:

let state = try await marmot.groupManagementState(accountRef: account, groupIdHex: group)
if state.leaveBlocked && state.canCancelLeave, await userChoosesCancel() {
    try await marmot.cancelLeave(accountRef: account, groupIdHex: group)
}

Undelivered Welcomes (optional)

pendingWelcomeDeliveries(accountRef) lists Welcomes still owed after a confirmed create or Add, oldest first (groupIdHex, messageIdHex, recipientHex, recordedAt, sizeClass). The event still fires once per process and Welcome; re-read the query for later causes. sizeClass diagnoses an observed all-relay size refusal; nil proves neither delivery nor non-delivery. MDK keeps retrying. See Undelivered Welcomes.

Account recovery status (optional)

accountRecoveryStatus(accountRef) returns the groups still catching up (catchingUpGroupIdsHex), whether the inbox is (inboxCatchingUp), and every notice (notices). Show the first two as "catching up" and re-read on RecoveryStatusChanged. See History may be incomplete notices.

Account-devices activation (optional)

An existing group gets the account-devices component only when an admin asks. Call accountDevicesActivation(accountRef, groupIdHex) and offer the action only on Eligible; otherwise explain NotAdmin, AlreadyEnabled, LegacyGroup, MembersNeedUpdate, DevicesNeedReplacement or DeviceLimitExceeded. The answer never names members. enableAccountDevices(accountRef, groupIdHex) sends one admin Commit that can never be undone, checks again, and fails with AccountDevicesActivationRefused and the same reason. Once enabled, clients older than 0.15 can no longer be invited into that group. See Turning on account devices.

Experimental device groups

Pairing, linked devices, sign-in review, compromise warnings, history transfer and backups are experimental: compiled only with the dev-device-groups build feature and enabled only through Marmot.newWithExperimentalDeviceGroups, marmot_client_new_with_experimental_device_groups or, in Rust, MarmotAppConfig::with_dev_device_groups(true). In ordinary builds and constructors their reads return empty, false or zero, their actions are refused (Runtime), and the experimental constructor returns experimental_device_groups_unavailable. Do not ship them. See Experimental device-group test builds.

C host changes

Recompile against the marmot.h shipped with the exact library. Input structs are read from host memory, so a mismatched header misreads silently; hand-written FFI declarations (ctypes, cgo, Dart) are not compiler-checked. Initialize input structs with {0}.

  • Removed: marmot_deployment_set_key_package_client_preference.
  • Mid-struct insertions (every later field moves): MarmotMediaAttachmentReference gains char *source_epoch_identity after source_epoch (input to every media and reaction send, marmot_download_media and marmot_build_media_imeta_tag; embedded in MarmotMediaRecord and MarmotMediaUploadAttachmentResult; pass it back exactly as returned). MarmotStickerRef *sticker follows tags_len in MarmotAppMessageRecord and MarmotReceivedMessage, kind in MarmotTimelineMessageRecord, MarmotChatListMessagePreview and MarmotTimelineReplyPreview, and preview_text in MarmotNotificationUpdate. MarmotTimelineMessageRecord gains bool recipient_confirmed between invalidation_status and client_token.
  • Trailing fields: MarmotClientOptions.device_platform; MarmotTimelineMessageQuery gains sender, has_since/since, has_until/until, uint32_t attachment_type (above 5 returns MARMOT_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT), uint8_t search_wall_clock and cursor_group_id; MarmotTimelineMessageRecord gains imported_from and history_import_provenance; plus MarmotAccountSummary.unlinked, the two new MarmotWipeOutcome fields, device_count on member records, MarmotAppGroupMlsState.convergence_parked, leave_blocked / can_cancel_leave on group, chat-row, management and capability records, and has_size_class/size_class on the WelcomeDeliveryPending event body. Structs that embed these by value (MarmotGroupDetails, MarmotCreatedGroup, MarmotPresentedChatRow, MarmotConversationHeader and others) change size.
  • Appended values: statuses 108–129 (MEDIA_REFERENCE_STALE_EPOCH 108 and _EPOCH_UNSETTLED 109, ACCOUNT_DEVICES_ACTIVATION_REFUSED 110, stickers 111–115, ACCOUNT_UNLINKED 116, GROUP_RECOVERY_UNSETTLED 117 and _SOURCE_MISMATCH 118, EVENT_TOO_LARGE 119, INVALID_CHAT_LIST_QUERY 120, emoji sets 121–128, LEAVE_NOT_BLOCKED 129); MarmotEvent_Tag 11–18; DEVICE_REMOVED in MarmotSelfMembership (3) and MarmotConversationParticipation (7); UNPROVEN_HISTORY (7) and BEFORE_REJOIN (8) in MarmotHistoryNoticeCause; QUEUED_INTENT_REFUSED (17) in MarmotGroupEventKind. Storage, size and media-epoch failures that returned RUNTIME (31), PUBLISH or INVALID_MEDIA_REFERENCE now return their typed status, as in Swift/Kotlin.

New functions mirror the features above (marmot_open_chat_list_query_window, marmot_chat_list_query_ids, marmot_revalidate_chat_list_query_ids, marmot_chat_list_ids, marmot_revalidate_chat_list_ids, marmot_cancel_leave, marmot_pending_welcome_deliveries, marmot_reaction_attachment, marmot_account_recovery_status, marmot_account_devices_activation, marmot_enable_account_devices, and the sticker and emoji-set families). Every new call blocks. Differences from Swift/Kotlin:

  • No structured error payloads: the chat-list query and activation refusal reasons, the EVENT_TOO_LARGE artifact and size class, and the EMOJI_SET_CHANGED current event id are only in the thread-local marmot_last_error_message; read it once, immediately.
  • Chat-list queries take a borrowed MarmotChatListViewQuery { view, filter, filter_len }; enums are uint32_t (out of range returns INVALID_CHAT_LIST_QUERY) and optional values use uint8_t presence flags.
  • MarmotEmojiSetInstallControl is host-owned: free it only after the install has returned and every other call on it has finished; cancel from another thread. See Emoji set installs.
  • marmot_reaction_attachment writes NULL with MARMOT_STATUS_OK when nothing is available; free a standalone result with marmot_attachment_entry_free, never an entry borrowed from a page.
  • sticker and history_import_provenance are freed by their parent record. marmot_sticker_ref_free, marmot_sticker_free, marmot_sticker_list_free and marmot_installed_custom_emoji_free are exported, but calling them on an embedded member is a double free.
  • Read size_class on the Welcome event and list only when has_size_class is set. marmot_cancel_leave allocates nothing.
  • marmot_client_new_with_experimental_device_groups exists in every build and returns MARMOT_STATUS_RUNTIME without the feature.

key_packages_deleted on MarmotWipeOutcome and MarmotSignOutOutcome is now 0 or 1, and MarmotRelayFailure.event_id_hex is empty when the failed deletion targeted the whole slot. See the C README (timeline search, blocked leaves) and the symbol inventory.

Rust host changes

  • Build. Building marmot-app or anything that depends on it needs Odin dev-2026-10 (revision 84bc3fc), because marmot-markdown parses Markdown in Odin. Install it with scripts/install-odin.sh or set ODIN; otherwise odin on PATH is used. Published MarmotKit, C and WN Agent artifacts are unaffected.
  • Crates. cgka-session is renamed marmot-session, and the runtime half of marmot-account (AccountDeviceRuntime, AccountError, MaintenanceTiming, KeyPackagePublisher, routing and effect types) moves there. Diagnostics exporters move to marmot-observability; old paths are re-exported except product_analytics::configure_product_analytics_from_environment, now marmot_app::configure_product_analytics_from_environment. Other new unpublished crates: marmot-pairing and marmot-markdown-ast.
  • Session. AccountDeviceRuntime::open(config, transport) is the only production constructor; ::new, session() and session_mut() need marmot-session's test-support feature. SessionError::Storage becomes SessionError::Engine(EngineError::Storage). A custom KeyPackagePublisher must implement withdraw_key_package_slot and delete_key_package_event, whose defaults return an error, or sign-out does not reach relays.
  • Errors and events. AppError gains 19 variants, including GroupInviteIncludesInviter, GroupCreateAdminNotMember, ExperimentalDeviceGroupsRequired, DeviceGroupRefused, InvalidChatListQuery, EventTooLarge (oversize transport and account errors now arrive as this) and the sticker and emoji-set errors. MarmotAppEvent gains the eight events above; HistoryNoticeCause, SelfMembership, ConversationParticipation, GroupEvent (QueuedIntentRefused, MessageReceived.sender_leaf_index) and RuntimePerformanceOperation gain variants or fields. These enums are exhaustive.
  • Records. TimelineMessageQuery gains sender, since, until, attachment_type (TimelineAttachmentType), search_wall_clock and cursor_group_id, and derives Default. MarmotAppConfig gains device_platform and dev_device_groups and loses dev_epoch_backfill_retry_backoff_ms and dev_fail_invite_welcome_intent. MarmotDeployment::key_package_client_preference and KeyPackageClientPreference are removed. ChatListWindowSnapshot loses first and last; open_chat_list_window takes impl Into<ChatListViewQuery>. MediaAttachmentOutcome::Accepted.reference is boxed. Struct literals add the fields listed in Required upgrade steps, plus AppCreateGroupOptions.initial_admins, ConversationAuthority.leave_blocked and admin_leave_steps_down, ConversationCapabilities.can_cancel_leave, and the session effect fields AutoPublish.welcomes, PublishFailure.oversized, WelcomeDeliveryFailure.size_class and KeyPackagePublishError.artifact_unusable. The marmot-app changelog lists every break. MarmotApp::group_push_debug_info is crate-private; the runtime's remains.
  • New methods. chat_list_ids, revalidate_chat_list_ids, cancel_leave, account_devices_activation, enable_account_devices, account_recovery_status, reaction_attachment and send_sticker on MarmotAppRuntime; sticker and emoji-set methods on MarmotApp.
  • Storage and engine traits. Third-party StorageProvider implementations add the AccountDeviceHistoryKeyStorage and DeviceGroupWelcomeStorage supertraits, GroupStorage::invitation_admission / put_invitation_admission, and pending_ref_high_water (monotonic, never lowered). CapabilityStorage::save_member_capabilities and member_capabilities are removed. CgkaEngine gains five required methods, TransportPeeler gains wrap_group_recovery, and SendIntent::AppMessage.expected_epoch is now Option<EpochPin>. None of the cgka_traits types is #[non_exhaustive]: SendIntent gains 12 variants (including StepDownAndLeave), SendResult gains LeaveRequested, EngineError gains 13 (including LeaveNotBlocked), and StoredMessagePayload::OutboundWelcome becomes a struct variant. Struct literals of Group, GroupMaintenanceState, KeyPackageLifecycleState, RetainedKeyPackagePrivateMaterial, DurableConvergencePass, AccountDeviceSignerBinding, AutoPublish and LeaveRequest add fields. The full lists are in the traits changelog. MULTI_DEVICE_JOIN_AUTHORIZATION_COMPONENT_ID is removed and CONSUMED_KEY_PACKAGE_RETENTION_SECS is renamed KEY_PACKAGE_REPLACEMENT_GRACE_SECS.
  • Transport. Replay capture (capture_replay, its types and ReplayEndpointView::capture_token) is removed; account history belongs to the recovery runner. NostrSdkNotification gains Disconnected and Replay.connected_at; DirectoryFetchOutcome gains complete_endpoints.
  • Account files. account.json and key-security.json are written owner-only; looser records are tightened on read, and a symlinked record is refused.

WN Agent and integrations

  • Protocol. The control protocol stays marmot.agent-control.v2 and only gains requests: group_create_capabilities (answered with initial_admins) and group_create_with_admins for founding co-admins; attachment_get, download_attachment and release_attachment for historical inbound attachments with leased local copies (release every lease; attachment_release_failed is retryable). AgentControlMediaRef gains optional source_epoch_identity. Rust AgentControlRequest/AgentControlResponse matches must handle the new variants.
  • Upgrade together. A 0.14.0 wn-agent closes the control socket without a reply on any request it cannot parse, including group_create_capabilities; treat that as "unsupported". Upgrade wn-agent and its Hermes, OpenClaw and terminal-harness plugins together.
  • OpenClaw. The plugin requires OpenClaw 2026.10.10 or newer (was 2026.7.1) and Node 24.22.1+ (24.x) or 26.12.1+ (was 22.19). The installer checks Node even with --no-configure-openclaw, and --yes runs openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities.
  • Connector-only install. scripts/install-wn-agent.sh installs and supervises wn-agent alone for your own control-socket client (home ~/.marmot-agents/standalone, service wn-agent-standalone / org.marmot.wn-agent.standalone), with --bootstrap or --import-identity. See custom clients.
  • Relays. wn-agent started without --relay reads MARMOT_RELAYS / MARMOT_RELAY and then falls back to the White Noise relays (0.14.0 started with none); --no-default-relays restores the old behavior. Installed services pass --relay and are unaffected. Startup adopts the account's published relay lists and publishes its own only when a complete read proves none exist; an inconclusive read fails with relay_list_inconclusive. wn-agent bootstrap --relay accepts comma-separated URLs.
  • Diagnostics. wn-agent doctor checks the home, socket, token, relays, accounts, daemon, protocol, KeyPackage and relay health (--json; nonzero exit on failure).
  • CLI. wn media send needs the complete media upload JSON, including source_epoch_identity; references rebuilt from media list fail with media_reference_stale_epoch. Timeline search gains --sender, --since, --until, --attachment-type and --cursor-group-id. wn daemon start waits up to 60 seconds; a daemon still migrating then is stopped with daemon_start_timeout, and the next start resumes the migrations. wnd no longer grows about 3 MB per request. Admin leave is refused until groups self-demote, as in the bindings.
  • Installers. Install only from the immutable wn-agent-v0.15.0 release with sibling .sha256 verification.

Changes requiring no new calls

  • Sends. Sends queued while offline publish after reconnect. A send never goes ahead of an intent queued earlier in the same group. A Welcome is published only once its Commit is, and every failed Welcome publish records a pending delivery. Failed convergence retries back off and park (convergenceParked; retryGroupConvergence resumes them). A queued intent the settled group refuses is retired with QueuedIntentRefused. Oversized events report EventTooLarge. Transfer-state changes are reported immediately.
  • Correctness. A write error while receiving a valid message no longer loses it; invite recovery and late group-record failures no longer leave stale rows; a member who left on a losing branch reaches the selected one; concurrent directory updates no longer erase relay lists; an accepted blockUser no longer reports BlockPublicationUncertain because the database was busy.
  • Performance. Idle maintenance ticks no longer open write transactions. Cached user search ranks in SQL and finds identities past the 10,000th. Dropping a MarmotApp without shutdown() frees its relay plane.
  • Privacy and security. Local forensic audit files expire 30 days after their last write. The pinned Nostr SDK rejects tampered events even when their id is cached, and directory events are verified before they are forwarded or stored. elliptic-curve/HPKE (RUSTSEC-2026-0387), openssl and the OpenClaw plugin's npm dependencies are updated.

The retired-relay denylist is unchanged.

Acceptance and remaining work

Before shipping an app on 0.15.0:

  • Compile against the matched artifacts with every host-built record and exhaustive switch/when updated; for C, rebuild every consumer.
  • Upgrade a real, large 0.14.0 account in place: time the first open, watch free disk and WAL size during it, then reopen and confirm the second open migrates nothing. Repeat with the app killed mid-upgrade, and with the notification extension as the first opener.
  • Interoperate with a 0.14.0 peer: an existing group keeps working; a new group with the 0.14.0 peer among its founders does not require the component; a 0.14.0 peer cannot be invited into a new 0.15-only group. Decide what your UI says then.
  • Test offline and cold start: queue sends offline, reconnect, and confirm they publish in order; confirm catch-up after a long absence and that accountRecoveryStatus clears.
  • Push to several devices of one account and to a newly added member.
  • Sign out an admin of a shared chat (step-down wait, cancellation); confirm only this device's KeyPackage is deleted. Decline as an admin invitee; Cancel a blocked leave.
  • Re-upload a media reference saved by 0.14.0, and exercise search filters (sender, date range, attachment type, non-ASCII text, wall-clock paging).
  • If adopted: select-all with revalidation and a text filter during the 0200 rewrite, emoji-set install cancellation, and account-devices activation.
  • Report evidence by stage: source, host smoke, packaged artifact, consuming app, real device.

What was validated: every change in this comparison landed through the merge queue's CI matrix, which includes the per-migration upgrade tests and the 0.10.4 account fixture upgraded through every migration with older-runner refusal; the binding-docs gate passes for the MarmotKit method and C symbol inventories at this source. Not validated here: upgrade time and disk use on a large 0.14.0 account, a schema-116 fixture from a 0.14.0 binary, device-level push across multiple devices, and app-level adoption on iOS or Android.

Known limitations:

  • Adding every device of an account is best effort: a device whose KeyPackage a relay does not return in time is left out until the account is invited again, lost devices are not re-added automatically, and an account for which one relay returns a full page (500) of KeyPackages or of KeyPackage deletion requests cannot be invited.
  • Right after a reconnect, a new send can still go out ahead of older unsent ones.
  • Migration 0175 refuses to open an account with an undecodable saved fanout or group evolution rather than guess.
  • A failed legacy group create in an earlier release can have left orphaned MLS state; 0.15 stops creating it but does not purge it.
  • The automatic-rejoin handshake's inner event kind is still under discussion in the specification (marmot#451).
  • Still open from 0.14.0: #2237 (a message more than five epochs late stays undecryptable without a notice); group-change prompts #2277, #2283, #2389 and #2286; #2253 (group data extension order); #2158 (an upload in flight across an epoch change is lost; its send now fails with the typed MediaReferenceStaleEpoch); and #1445 (WN Agent's control socket grants its whole API to any authenticated client).
